No original-site assets or model payloads were downloaded, and no browser session or upstream script was run in this review.

name: NJFE: a Soulear camera protocol bridge for desktop inspection
description_en: Reuses otoscope's reverse-engineered i4season/Soulear protocol in an ESP32-C3 bridge and Python desktop viewer. The author credits Claude Code for implementation and reports streaming one Hopefox Find T to a Windows PC, with recording, orientation and LED controls.
description_zh: 在 ESP32-C3 桥接器与 Python 电脑查看器中复用 otoscope 经逆向得到的 i4season／Soulear 协议。作者将实现归功于 Claude Code 辅助，报告把一台 Hopefox Find T 的视频传到 Windows 电脑，并提供录像、方向调整及 LED 控制。
requirements: The input is the camera's Wi-Fi i4season/Soulear UDP traffic. An ESP32-C3 SuperMini with the documented 0.42-inch, 72×40 SSD1306 OLED reassembles JPEG frames and forwards them with accelerometer metadata over custom USB CDC serial to the supplied Python viewer. This is not a UVC webcam output; the camera's own USB port is described as charge-only. No vendor-camera firmware or complete companion-app source is recovered.

The documented build uses PlatformIO espressif32 6.11.0, Arduino core 2.0.17 and U8g2 ^2.35.30. The desktop tools require Python with Tkinter plus pyserial >=3.5, opencv-python >=4.8, NumPy >=1.24 and Pillow >=12.3.0. The project reports Windows testing; it does not establish support for every desktop OS or compatible-looking ear camera.

The README and NOTICE credit rbeilvert/otoscope by rubec for the packet format, commands, frame assembly and accelerometer/rotation logic. That project documents reverse engineering Soulear's libWifiCamera.so. NJFE reports Claude Code assistance across research, implementation, tools and documentation, with the human supplying hardware, decisions and device testing. This does not establish Claude as the original protocol discoverer, or any REA involvement; NJFE does not pin the exact otoscope revision it borrowed.

The author reports one Hopefox Find T with HKV41B firmware, 480×480 JPEG at about 17 fps, plus photos, MJPG AVI recording, rotation and LED control. The public --test N viewer mode receives and decodes N live frames, saves the last image and prints frame rate; it needs the hardware. The reviewed tree has no separate offline conformance-fixture suite. These reports and source-level framing checks do not establish full protocol compatibility; this collection did not run the tools or reproduce the hardware result.

The camera network remains open and unauthenticated. SECURITY.md states that the bridge accepts UDP traffic without source authentication and can receive injected images or replies; serial access is trusted and recordings are stored unencrypted. A local USB bridge does not remove these camera-network limitations. The project describes an inspection tool, not a medical device for diagnosis or treatment.

NJFE declares GPL-3.0-or-later in its README, NOTICE and REUSE metadata, and identifies protocol code and roll calculation derived from GPL otoscope. Third-party build/runtime libraries retain their own licenses. Public source review does not grant rights to vendor software or images; no proprietary app, firmware binary, image capture, device or upstream runtime was used in this review.

name: BaoCut Slides: adapting an interactive web editor
description_en: Documents BaoCut’s interactive slide editor, whose author says the implementation draws on Claude Slides. It adds a local deck store, HTML/CSS compiler and annotation-to-agent bridge for browser and desktop hosts; the design reports a Web-flow check, without establishing original backend recovery or full behavioral parity.
description_zh: 记录 BaoCut 交互式幻灯片编辑器，作者称其实现借鉴自 Claude Slides。它为浏览器与桌面宿主加入本地文稿存储、HTML/CSS 编译器及标注到智能体的桥接；设计说明报告了 Web 流程检查，但未确立原有后端恢复或完整行为一致性。
requirements: This entry covers the pinned Slides component, whose author says the implementation draws on Claude Slides, not the whole BaoCut product. It contains an editor runtime, a restricted HTML/CSS slide compiler and a new BaoCut host. Decks use a v4 deck.json index, per-slide HTML and local assets. The reviewed design/runtime notes do not identify the exact Claude Slides release or extraction record; they do not establish a clean-room process or recovery of Anthropic’s original hosted backend.

Building the editor requires Node.js >=22.12.0, npm workspace dependencies and the apps/slides-editor build; a BaoCut Runtime/host supplies file, annotation and download capabilities. The runtime declares React ^19.3.0 and PptxGenJS 3.12.0 with project patches. Full BaoCut source builds also require Rust/Cargo, CMake and platform C++ tools; Apple Silicon native inference needs full Xcode/Metal. Agent-driven deck creation requires a configured agent engine such as Codex CLI or Claude Code, with its own account and service terms.

The documented implementation is single-user and file-backed: it supports local saves with version/conflict checks, asset routes and external-change notifications. Conflict checks precede writes; individual-file writes do not establish whole-batch transactional rollback. Shared rooms/presence, share links, persistent comment threads and sending to Google Drive/Google Slides are explicitly out of scope. External updates may reload the editor and lose selection/scroll position. Export code exists, but the design still places PPTX/PDF downloads in P1; these documents do not establish complete export compatibility.

The design note reports end-to-end Web annotation validation and explicitly says Electron was not tested for that flow. Published tests exercise local file publication/conflicts, HTTP read/write boundaries and annotation forwarding; some host tests use fake fetch and agent-harness tests use a fake driver. HTML/CSS compiler and round-trip checks are skipped when the built compiler is unavailable. These are implementation tests, not an original-Claude differential oracle or proof of full visual/behavioral parity; this collection did not run them.

The root BaoCut Community License 1.0 is source-available: it permits stated personal/internal uses and content creation, while commercialization of the software/code or commercial hosting needs a separate license. Third-party components keep their own terms, including the documented PptxGenJS MIT and embedded mediabunny MPL-2.0 notices. Those dependency notices do not establish reuse rights in any reused Claude material or the bundled icon font; the runtime notes say that font needs replacement. This source review does not supply such rights or treat the whole component as permissively open source.

BaoCut documents agent-assisted creation and annotation workflows, but the reviewed case sources do not establish which model produced the adaptation or any REA involvement. Support for Claude Code/Codex as agent engines is not evidence of the reconstruction method. Use independently authorized slide content and respect external asset/font terms. This review inspected pinned source and test definitions without running the app, models or checks, or retrieving bundled fonts, media or application packages.

name: Pocket Tasks: reconstructing task state and persistence
description_en: A teaching case with disclosed prior source access carries a REA-assisted investigation of a small command-line app into a separate Node implementation. It preserves observed task editing, persistence and selection behavior, then compares scoped outputs against fixed expectations and captured reference sessions.
description_zh: 此教学案例明确披露作者先前接触过源码，将一次 REA 辅助的小型命令行应用调查推进为另行编写的 Node 实现。它保留所观察到的任务编辑、持久保存及选择行为，再将限定范围的输出与固定期望值及捕获的参考会话比较。
requirements: Pocket Tasks 1.0.0 is an authored local command-line app, not a commercial application or a native-binary benchmark. Its separate Node.js 20+ candidate implements nine commands and schema-1 JSON storage, including saved/draft separation, explicit save, cancel, restart and the original row-position selection quirk. It needs only the Node standard library and disposable local stores; there is no graphical interface or network backend.

The historical investigation combines REA JavaScript source analysis, ordinary source inspection and recorded process/file observations. The sanitized REA excerpt identifies the same target bytes but retains unknown semantic coverage and 230 semantic unknowns. It is not a canonical Evidence bundle or independent attestation, and parsing coverage is not behavioral equivalence. The later Node validator does not repeat that REA session.

The author had already seen the target source, reviewer scenarios, tests and prior answers before implementation. The candidate imports only Node filesystem/path modules; a published test definition copies its file alone before checking save behavior. Runtime independence from the reference does not establish independent discovery, a blind trial, clean-room provenance or an agent/model performance result.

The saved report records 16/16 checker process sessions across 12 scenarios and 10/10 replays of captured observations across seven scenarios. These overlap and must not be counted as 26 independent observations. The checker uses fixed, hand-authored expectations; responses and saved JSON are compared semantically, while malformed stores and foreign pending files use byte-preservation checks where required. The report retains humanReview=pending, reaTrial=unverified and independentEvaluation=false; these are author-reported results, not rerun by this collection.

The six recorded target/candidate/observation/validator/checker/packet-tool hashes and the oracle digest match the reviewed source. The report’s TASK.md packet hash instead matches an earlier instruction revision: a later edit changed review/authorization wording without changing the behavioral contract. Treat the packet record as historical evidence, not fresh validation of every file in the current package. The failure history also retains an initial restricted-Windows attempt with five passes and four failures, followed by nine passes with unchanged candidate code in a permitted local environment.

The contract bounds each invocation to 64 commands and 65,536 UTF-8 bytes, stores to 32 tasks and titles to 80 UTF-16 code units. Coverage is limited to named behaviors and tests; concurrent writers, crash durability, hostile filesystem races, UI behavior, hidden backends and production performance are outside the parity claim. MIT covers the authored example; upstream REA and other linked material remain separate. No target, candidate, checker, installer, model or upstream test was executed in this review.

name: Open Scrantic: reconstructing the Johnny Castaway screensaver engine
description_en: Reconstructs the Johnny Castaway screensaver engine in Rust, with author-disclosed REA and Claude Code use. It reads original files to run recovered animation scripts and calendar-based story state on modern desktops; documented deviations and limited tests stop short of complete behavioral equivalence.
description_zh: 以 Rust 重建 Johnny Castaway 屏幕保护程序引擎，作者明确披露使用 REA 与 Claude Code。它读取原始文件，在现代桌面上运行恢复的动画脚本及按日历推进的故事状态；文档保留实现差异与有限测试范围，未确立完整行为等价。
requirements: Reviewed at v0.3.0: this is a Windows 3.1 screensaver-engine reconstruction, not a game port. The author reports recovering formats and TTM/ADS script semantics from disassembly, with human-directed REA/Claude Code work and comparisons against the original. Those reports do not establish exhaustive parity or an independent agent-performance result.

Builds pin Rust 1.99.1; Cargo declares minimum Rust 1.99 and edition 2024. The project targets Windows, macOS and Linux using winit, softbuffer and rodio. Linux builds also require ALSA development headers and pkg-config.

Runtime requires separately obtained SCRANTIC.SCR, RESOURCE.MAP and RESOURCE.001 beside the executable. README sizes and SHA-256 values identify the expected original files; the loader instead checks known executable strings/layout, not whole-file hashes. Arbitrary original builds are unsupported. Options and story state use SCRANTIC.INI, saved on normal exit.

Deliberate differences include full-frame redraw, potentially one-pixel line/ellipse differences, bounded final-scene selection and a fixed two-second title display. Optional dedithering and softened audio default off. The original settings dialog and password feature are absent, as are unused animated-palette, 256-color and ADS-variable features.

The headless test runs 6,000 steps and requires three completed scenes, without original-frame comparison. Data-dependent tests silently return when OPEN_SCRANTIC_DATA is unset; other tests cover parsing and arithmetic. CI checks formatting, lint, three-platform builds and --version, not cargo test or original-data playback. Snapshot output supports inspection, not an automated original-output oracle.

MIT covers project source, not original executable content, art, scripts or sounds, which users must supply with appropriate authorization. The author describes independent, non-commercial interoperability without Sierra/Dynamix endorsement. This collection reviewed sources and test definitions; it did not reproduce the implementation or results.

name: Eleven
description_en: An agent-first desktop reverse-engineering app that opens Mach-O, ELF and PE binaries, Android packages and GPU kernels, and lets any Agent Client Protocol agent read code, rename functions, add notes and propose patches in a shared window. Native code is decompiled by Ghidra through a bundled REA build, with Rizin and jadx as alternative engines. It is a workbench around existing engines, not a new decompiler or a reconstruction case.
description_zh: 以智能体为核心的桌面逆向工程应用，可打开 Mach-O、ELF、PE 二进制、Android 安装包和 GPU 内核，让任何支持 Agent Client Protocol 的智能体在同一窗口中阅读代码、重命名函数、添加笔记并提出补丁。原生代码通过内置的 REA 构建交由 Ghidra 反编译，也可改用 Rizin 和 jadx。它是围绕现有引擎的工作台，并非新的反编译器或重建案例。
requirements: Reviewed version 0.1.9 (release dated 2026-10-16) targets macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon, Windows x64 and Linux x64. The documented macOS and Windows installers pipe a remote script into the shell; macOS builds are not notarized, so the installer clears the download quarantine. Users supply the apps, binaries or APKs they analyze.

Native analysis uses Ghidra 12.x with Java 21 through REA, or Rizin for faster opening; first-run setup downloads missing engines or reuses local copies, and Ghidra is not bundled. Android packages need jadx, with apktool optional for smali. Building from source needs Bun, Node 20+, Ghidra, a JDK and a REA 6.x checkout; the release workflow builds REA from the Zfinix/rea fork’s feat/set-code-type branch rather than an upstream release.

Agents connect over the Agent Client Protocol, including the README’s Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor and Copilot options; model access, cost and data handling follow the chosen agent. Agents receive Eleven’s own MCP server and an eleven-rea proxy that passes REA tools through but redirects REA’s name, comment, bookmark and code-type writes into Eleven’s project. Per-tool Allow/Ask/Never permissions and privacy prompts are settings; this collection did not audit what reaches an agent’s service.

Byte patches are written to a copy, agent patches arrive as suggestions, and project changes are logged with their author and can be undone. CI at the reviewed commit runs typechecks on Ubuntu and macOS; the Ghidra-backed test suite is a separate local script. This review read source and documentation without installing the app, running agents or analyzing a target.

Eleven is Apache-2.0; the bundled REA and Node.js keep their MIT and other licenses, and agent logos remain their owners’ trademarks. The tool grants no rights to analyze, patch or redistribute third-party software, and its outputs are agent-assisted analysis rather than verified source recovery.

name: Flutter build identification
description_en: Identifies a Flutter APK’s Dart snapshot hash, per-ABI library digests and engine build provenance, then inspects one ABI’s AOT snapshot sections, through REA’s pure-parsing CLI and MCP tools. The string-pool output is a bounded byte-pattern projection of package and SDK URIs, not deserialized Dart classes or recovered source.
description_zh: 通过 REA 的纯解析命令行与 MCP 工具，识别 Flutter APK 的 Dart 快照哈希、各 ABI 库摘要与引擎构建来源，再检查单个 ABI 的 AOT 快照段。字符串池输出是对 package 与 SDK URI 的有界字节模式投影，并非反序列化的 Dart 类或恢复的源码。
requirements: Reviewed on main as rea-agents 6.7.0, which declares Node ^22.19.0, ^24.11.0 or 26+. identify-flutter-build and inspect-dart-aot (MCP identify_flutter_build and inspect_dart_aot) parse a caller-supplied APK’s libapp.so and libflutter.so without an engine, external tool, execution or network lookup. Inputs are copied into an owned read-only snapshot, with documented bounds such as 2 GiB per APK and 256 MiB per library.

REA performs no hash-to-SDK lookup; mapping a snapshot hash to a Dart release needs an external dataset such as reFlutter’s. Complete structural coverage currently requires the FullAOT kind of the supported Dart 2.14 snapshot layout, and other kinds are kept with partial coverage. Typed class and function recovery needs an SDK-specific parser, and class-like tokens include incidental matches.

The documented verifier runs both tools through the compiled CLI and stdio MCP on the Flutter Gallery 2.9.2 release APK against a pinned expectations file: one agreeing snapshot hash on all three ABIs, engine labels and URI counts. A plain aapt2-built APK checks negative detection. The guide reports the Gallery workflow and 147 focused tests passing on macOS 14.8.9 x86-64 and Windows 11 x64 guests.

In merged PR #1582, an independent reviewer reports that hashes, ELF sections and package lists matched readelf/strings checks on three F-Droid apps, PocketDhamma, Flutter McSweepy and cone, on pre-merge heads, with a non-Flutter control not detected; the thread records fixes for gaps found. These checks cover build identity and structure, not app-logic reconstruction. REA declares MIT; analysed APKs keep their own licenses, and this collection did not run REA or any APK.

name: Static HarmonyOS package inventory
description_en: Inventories HarmonyOS HAP, HSP and App Pack files through REA’s hardened ZIP reader and projects an execution-free application graph: component paths, IDs and hashes, Stage/FA packaging hints, runtime-family hints and path-based native-bridge hypotheses. Every claim rests on path presence; manifests, Ark bytecode, resources and signatures are not decoded or verified.
description_zh: 通过 REA 加固的 ZIP 读取器清点 HarmonyOS 的 HAP、HSP 与 App Pack 文件，并投影出无需执行的应用图：组件路径、ID 与哈希、Stage／FA 打包模型提示、运行时类别提示，以及基于路径的原生桥接假设。所有结论仅基于路径存在；清单、Ark 字节码、资源和签名均未被解码或验证。
requirements: Reviewed on main as rea-agents 6.7.0, which declares Node ^22.19.0, ^24.11.0 or 26+. No HarmonyOS SDK, toolchain or engine is needed: inspect-artifact produces the inventory and project-harmony-application-graph (MCP project_harmony_application_graph) projects it, with CLI and MCP sharing one workflow. .hap, .hsp and ZIP-verified root .app inputs are recognized; .har shared libraries are deferred because the suffix also names HTTP Archive JSON.

Outputs are path-presence claims: Stage is inferred only from module.json and FA only from config.json, App Pack children are listed without recursive inventory, encrypted or unavailable entries make coverage partial, and N-API bridge entries are hypotheses. Manifest semantics, Ark bytecode contents and versions, resource resolution, signing verification and observed native boundaries stay listed as limitations, and inventories that cannot be authenticated fail closed.

The verification lane downloads a SHA-256-pinned harmony-next-pipeline 1.0.1 HAP from an MIT-licensed source repository into an ignored directory and checks inventory authenticity, projection determinism, Stage path hints, exact component sets, complete coverage and CLI/MCP parity. The fixture’s compiler/SDK versions and reproducible build are not established, the lane does not complete the pinned-toolchain acceptance in roadmap issue #1431, and missing META-INF entries do not establish signing status.

REA declares MIT. Analysed packages keep their own licenses, and the guide says the fixture’s bundled component licenses were not independently audited; the downloaded artifact is not redistributed. Merged PR #1447 introduced this increment. This collection did not run REA or any package.

name: MIPS ELF analysis through Ghidra
description_en: Documents REA’s Ghidra lane for MIPS ELF executables, relocatable objects and MIPS16 shared images, including a pinned 32-bit language for recordless legacy firmware executables that Ghidra would otherwise import as 64-bit. Admission is bounded by declared header and ABI-record facts, and verification compares source-owned fixtures with independent readelf output rather than executing or rehosting firmware.
description_zh: 说明 REA 通过 Ghidra 分析 MIPS ELF 可执行文件、可重定位目标文件与 MIPS16 共享镜像的流程，包括为缺少 ABI 记录的旧式固件可执行文件固定 32 位语言，以免 Ghidra 将其按 64 位导入。准入以文件头声明和 ABI 记录为界；验证将项目自有的测试样本与独立的 readelf 输出对照，而不执行或重新托管固件。
requirements: Needs a caller-installed Ghidra and compatible JDK on a supported Linux or macOS host; Windows Ghidra P0 does not admit MIPS, and Hopper/IDA gain no MIPS support. The lane does not execute MIPS code or rehost firmware. The standard profile admits ELF32 executables and relocatable objects declaring o32 and MIPS32r2; MIPS16 shared images have a separate bounded profile. ELF64, n32/n64, microMIPS, machine variants, FP64, NAN2008 and PSP PRX are refused.

Merged PR #1898, for issue #1620, admits recordless legacy ELF32 executables with EF_MIPS_ARCH_32 or 32R2, an unspecified ABI field and an inspected absence of ABI-flags records. It pins MIPS:<LE|BE>:32:default and checks the language Ghidra reports after import. o32 is recorded as an analysis assumption, not a declared fact, and floating-point ABI semantics stay unverified.

Optional real-provider lanes need caller-supplied Clang with MIPS targets, LLD, GNU readelf or MIPS cross-binutils, and Ghidra. They build source-owned fixtures in both byte orders without executing them, comparing instruction bytes, symbols, languages and relocations with independent readelf facts. The guide states that pseudocode presence and decoding agreement do not establish runtime, delay-slot or complete floating-point semantics.

The issue author reports gating a local patch on four real MIPS32 LE firmware ELFs whose function entries matched separate 32-bit Ghidra exports, and 400 of 5,250 functions lost on one image under auto-selection; those files are not public. A PR reviewer tested header-edited OpenWrt kernels and BusyBox builds with Capstone cross-checks and found no unedited public recordless file. No device model, firmware change or runtime behavior is established.

REA declares MIT. Ghidra, compilers, binutils and analysed firmware keep their own terms, and the firmware behind the author’s results is not supplied. This collection reviewed the issue, PR thread and pinned sources without running REA, Ghidra or any target.

name: PSP static ELF analysis through Ghidra
description_en: Documents REA’s bounded Ghidra profile for static PSP ELF executables, which leaves Allegrex instructions, PSP loading and calling conventions to a caller-installed ghidra-allegrex extension while reusing REA’s CLI, MCP, Evidence and snapshot workflows. It admits one PSPSDK header and ABI declaration on Linux x64 and verifies selected static facts on a self-built fixture, not commercial games or PRX modules.
description_zh: 说明 REA 针对静态 PSP ELF 可执行文件的受限 Ghidra 配置：Allegrex 指令、PSP 加载与调用约定交由使用者安装的 ghidra-allegrex 扩展处理，同时沿用 REA 的命令行、MCP、证据与快照流程。它仅在 Linux x64 上接受一种 PSPSDK 文件头与 ABI 声明，并在自行构建的测试样本上验证选定的静态事实，不涉及商业游戏或 PRX 模块。
requirements: The initial profile runs on a Linux x64 host and admits little-endian ELF32 executables with the PSPSDK declaration e_flags 0x10a23001 and an inspected version-0 ABI-flags record matching the documented single-float Allegrex declarations. PRX, relocatable or shared images, PBP/ISO/CSO containers, emulation and live overlays are out of scope; missing or different declarations are refused, and file names do not identify a target.

Install a compatible ghidra-allegrex extension inside the selected Ghidra distribution; REA never downloads, installs, rebuilds or vendors it, and fingerprints its files before launch. The published compatibility pairing is Ghidra 12.1.3, extension v21.4, PSPDEV v20261001 and JDK 21; other builds that pass the metadata check are not described as independently verified. Missing prerequisites return PSP_EXTENSION_UNAVAILABLE without fallback.

Verification uses the real MIPS verifier’s PSP mode with caller-supplied PSPDEV tools. A maintained fixture built from tests/conformance/psp is analysed without execution and checked against PSP GNU tool observations: known functions, a direct call, an immediate, BITREV, a global word, snapshot reopening and an A-B-A target switch. Merged PR #1599 reports a passing real-Ghidra run on an earlier contribution head and says the final head was not freshly revalidated by that run.

These are selected static facts, not behavioral equivalence, complete VFPU semantics or general compatibility with commercial PSP executables; the extension does not fully model VFPU prefix effects. No commercial game data is used or reconstructed, and issue #1330 remains open. REA declares MIT; ghidra-allegrex, Ghidra, PSPDEV and analysed executables keep their own terms. This collection ran nothing.

name: Touhou reconstructions: an agent-driven method across three games
description_en: An essay published on REA’s site, with pinned evidence notes, describes one author’s agent-driven reconstructions of TH08, TH095 and TH04. It dates milestones from public commits and progress ledgers, separates exact-comparison and playable-build oracles, and documents a TH08 check that missed wrong floating-literal data. Project results remain author-reported, and REA is credited with supplying analysis evidence, not the reconstructions themselves.
description_zh: REA 网站发表的一篇文章及其固定版本的证据说明，介绍一位作者以智能体驱动重建 TH08、TH095 与 TH04 的过程。文章依据公开提交与进度记录标注里程碑，区分精确比对与可游玩构建两类判定依据，并记录 TH08 一项检查漏查错误浮点字面量数据的问题。项目结果仍为作者报告；REA 的作用是为智能体提供分析证据，而非完成重建本身。
requirements: The evidence notes, checked on 10 October 2026, treat three separate projects: a continuation of GensokyoClub’s TH08 1.00d reconstruction, a TH095 1.02a reconstruction started from zero confirmed functions, and a PC-98 TH04 reconstruction crediting ReC98. Milestone intervals use public commit timestamps and measure recorded spacing, not compute time, effort or a controlled speedup.

Pinned ledgers report 1,106 of 1,107 TH08 functions accepted, 696 exact TH095 functions out of 697 confirmed, and 661 exact TH04 functions out of 663 reviewed candidates, each under its own definitions; the notes warn against cross-game rates or whole-executable completion percentages. TH08 Linux and Web ports, a playable TH095 Windows i386 build and four TH04 DOS products are recorded milestones. TH04 play results rest on the maintainer’s manual observations, and its 64-bit port is in development.

In TH08, an instruction-byte comparison accepted source using 0.0 where the original executable used 128.0, because it did not check the referenced literal data. TH08 PRs #11 and #13 added literal-data checks and corrected twelve more stale references among 1,548 audited. The website work reexamined history and metadata without rerunning the historical compiler or game.

The essay and notes supply no game files, compilers or builds; each project’s repository documents its own original-game and toolchain requirements, and game rights stay with their owners. GensokyoClub’s TH08 history keeps its attribution and license, and its public policy excluding AI-primary contributions is paraphrased rather than adopted. TH08 has a separate catalog record; this review did not separately review the TH095 or TH04 repositories or run any project.

REA is described as supplying analysis evidence to agents; the projects also used their own analysis bridges and tooling, and historical results are not relabeled as REA output. The author presents the method and its industrial analogy as an account and argument, not a measured agent-versus-human comparison or proof that it transfers to other fields.

name: TicTacToe-AI: a bounded REA-fork reconstruction of one game method
description_en: The author’s REA fork, posted as rea-engine and since renamed RE-Agent, decompiles the shipped .NET executable of the GPL-licensed TicTacToe-AI game, recompiles the recovered C# and resources, and repairs one decompiler error against the original IL. A differential probe runs original and rebuilt code on all 19,683 board assignments for one status method and compares six form renders. The report passes only that method; the whole game remains partial.
description_zh: 作者的 REA 分叉（发帖时名为 rea-engine，后更名为 RE-Agent）反编译 GPL 许可的 TicTacToe-AI 游戏所发布的 .NET 可执行文件，重新编译恢复出的 C# 与资源，并依据原始 IL 修复一处反编译错误。差分探针在一个状态判定方法的全部 19,683 种棋盘赋值上运行原版与重建代码，并比较六张窗体渲染图。报告只判定该方法通过，整个游戏仍属部分重建。
requirements: The reviewed develop commit (2026-10-15) reports Feature PASS for CheckGameStatus over its declared 3^9 board domain and PARTIAL for the whole game. AI move selection and RNG, menus, timing and sound are unverified, the executables are not byte-identical, and raw terminal captures differ by one carriage return. The posts’ “byte for byte” wording therefore applies to structured board records and six render PNGs, not to the program.

The input is the published TicTacToe-AI executable from tatlead’s GPL-3.0 repository, identified by SHA-256 in the report. The repository redistributes it with the GPL text and a source archive kept for license compliance; the statement that this source was not consulted during reconstruction is author-reported.

The fork needs Node.js 22.19+ or 24.11+; recovery uses ilspycmd plus a host Roslyn compiler and Mono references, with script defaults pointing at Homebrew paths on macOS. Verification needs a local X11 display and Mono/libgdiplus. The recorded run used macOS 15.3.1 on ARM64 with Xvfb, so both renders come from the same Mono runtime rather than native Windows.

Scripts recover a fresh replica, then a probe executes the original and rebuilt assemblies, compares return values and indicator bytes for every board, and captures Form.DrawToBitmap images after button sequences. The current result JSON records zero board-record mismatches and terminalBytesEqual false. This collection read the reports and scripts without running the executables, tools or probe.

The fork is MIT with morluto’s REA copyright retained and lists optional engines such as Ghidra and Frida under their own licenses; the game and its reconstruction carry GPL-3.0 obligations. Fork-specific code is not part of upstream REA releases, and the repository was renamed after the posts, whose rea-engine link now redirects to RE-Agent.

name: REA in Claude Code: an isolated static-analysis A/B trial
description_en: A Japanese field report connects REA 6.4.0 to Claude Code in a separate project directory, denies 43 of its 170 tools and common shell launch forms, and compares REA-enabled and REA-disabled runs on two real tasks: an Electron terminal’s packaged files and a saved HAR capture. Both arms answered correctly, while the REA arm took up to 2.00× the time and 1.67× the API-equivalent cost. It is an analysis-evaluation and safety-configuration case, not a reconstruction.
description_zh: 一篇日文实践报告在单独的项目目录中把 REA 6.4.0 接入 Claude Code，屏蔽其 170 个工具中的 43 个以及常见的命令行启动方式，并在两个真实任务上比较启用与禁用 REA 的运行：一个 Electron 终端的分发文件，以及一份保存的 HAR 通信记录。两组都给出正确答案，而启用 REA 的一组耗时最多为 2.00 倍、按 API 计价的费用最多为 1.67 倍。这是分析评估与安全配置案例，而非重建案例。
requirements: The article by keigoly was published on Zenn on 2026-10-14 (JST). It pins REA 6.4.0 from the rea-agents package and runs it with a checksum-verified official Node.js 24.21.0 placed inside the project, because the host’s Homebrew Node 25.8.1 is outside REA’s supported range. All trials used non-interactive claude -p with Claude Opus 5.5 and permission prompts bypassed; the Claude Code version is not stated.

Isolation is configuration, not a sandbox: REA is enabled only through a project-local .mcp.json, a generated deny list blocks 43 tools selected from effect metadata, and Bash prefix rules block common package-runner launches. The author states that deny rules are a fence rather than isolation, that other invocation forms bypass the prefix rules, and that prompt injection through analysis output was not tested.

The tasks were MIT-licensed Orca terminal v1.4.224 (128 MB of distributed Electron files) and a 2.5 MB HAR from an unnamed venue website; answers were checked against Orca’s public source and the HAR data. The author excluded DRM or license circumvention, online multiplayer games, business or customer data and malware from scope.

Each condition ran once (n=1), the REA arm was told to prefer REA tools, parallel processes make timings approximate, and only static JavaScript/web work with one model was tested; an interrupted run was excluded and repeated. One REA analysis result exceeded the 10 MB MCP response limit. Scripts and JSONL logs are excerpted rather than published, so this collection could not and did not rerun the trials.

The author reports that REA helped with extraction, such as asar unpacking and HAR element extraction, while grep and small scripts carried code reading in both arms. Nothing was reconstructed: the HAR task identified an existing request path. Native binaries and APKs are deferred to a planned second step; Orca, the venue site, REA and the model service keep their own terms.

name: NativeAOT metadata recovery with Ghidra
description_en: Recovers .NET 8 NativeAOT metadata from x64 PE executables during REA’s Ghidra analysis: MethodTable relationships, virtual slots and frozen strings from RTR 9.1 data, through a built-in read-only parser or an optional headless adapter that annotates the Ghidra database. Generated names, inferred prototypes and recovered native pseudocode stay separate from the unknown original C# names, fields and source.
description_zh: 在 REA 的 Ghidra 分析中，从 x64 PE 可执行文件恢复 .NET 8 NativeAOT 元数据：通过内置只读解析器或可选的无界面适配器（会为 Ghidra 数据库添加注释），从 RTR 9.1 数据中取得 MethodTable 关系、虚表槽位与冻结字符串。生成的名称、推断的原型和恢复的原生伪代码，与未知的原始 C# 名称、字段和源码明确区分。
requirements: Reviewed on main as rea-agents 6.7.0, which declares Node ^22.19.0, ^24.11.0 or 26+. Bring your own Ghidra and JDK; the guide’s Windows check used Ghidra 12.1.4 and JDK 21. The built-in parser handles x64 PE32+ with .NET 8 RTR 9.1 metadata and needs a unique RTR header and exactly one DEHYDRATED_DATA row; other RTR versions and PE architectures are reported as unsupported or partial. Ordinary PE/CLI or ReadyToRun assemblies belong to REA’s managed-code tools instead.

The optional adapter is built from a clean pinned checkout of Washi1337/ghidra-nativeaot with existing git, javac and jar; REA records the JAR’s SHA-256, copies it and rechecks the digest before loading, and JARs run inside Ghidra, so supply a trusted build. It annotates within an ephemeral Program transaction and never changes the original executable. It is unavailable on Windows Ghidra P0, where database tools do not see rehydrated bytes and slot targets come from the parser report.

Outputs include MethodTable addresses, base types, interfaces, virtual slots and frozen strings, within documented local limits such as 128 MiB of captured PE bytes and 4 MiB of report JSON; rows beyond the report budget are omitted with partial coverage. Type identification uses upstream heuristics and prototypes remain inferences. Pseudocode is recovered native logic, not original C# source, and original class/member names and custom field layouts stay unknown.

Verification uses benign source-built .NET 8.0.22 fixtures with independent compiler/linker-symbol and directory-byte oracles, plus stripped and negative inputs; fixtures are never executed, and building them needs .NET SDK 8.0.416 and platform NativeAOT tools. The real MCP lane runs only on Linux x64 with the adapter. Windows-host behavior was checked manually once on Windows 11 x64 without the JAR against the fixture oracle and linker map; no CI lane repeats that check.

REA declares MIT. The parser’s hydration semantics are adapted from Washi1337/ghidra-nativeaot (MIT, with its notice shipped under licenses/) and cross-checked against .NET’s MethodTable.h. Analysed executables keep their own licenses. Merged PR #748 introduced the integration and issue #744 records the request and its closure without claiming C# project reconstruction. This collection did not run REA, Ghidra or any fixture.

name: UltraSunnyMoon: a partial, REA-led Pokémon Ultra Sun reconstruction
description_en: The author uses a pinned REA build with Ghidra to analyze a user-supplied Pokémon Ultra Sun base executable, rebuild it byte for byte from split objects, and swap in two small compiled C runtime routines. Both replacements are behavior-tested but nonmatching and every other byte stays original; one recorded input movie drives the original and hybrid builds to the same bedroom movement in the Azahar emulator. Retail compiler identity, exact matching, module loading and broader gameplay remain open.
description_zh: 作者使用固定版本的 REA 与 Ghidra，分析使用者自备的《宝可梦 究极之日》基础版可执行文件，由拆分出的对象逐字节重建该文件，并替换进两个编译后的小型 C 运行时例程。两处替换均经行为测试但与原字节不一致，其余字节均保持原样；同一段录制输入在 Azahar 模拟器中让原版与混合构建到达相同的卧室移动场景。零售编译器识别、精确匹配、模块加载及更广泛的游戏行为仍待解决。
requirements: README reports that the original and combined rebuilt games reproduce controllable bedroom gameplay, that both C replacements are behavior-tested but nonmatching, and that no completion percentage is claimed. STATUS.md (updated 2026-10-12) lists an unchanged main executable and one CRO module rebuilt byte for byte, the integrated __aeabi_vec_ctor_nocookie_nodtor helper and a 36-byte startup BSS clearer. The hybrid builds still contain mostly original code and assets and need a 3DS runtime; a native PC port is a later phase.

Requires the user’s own Ultra Sun base version 0 container (title 00040000001b5000, product code CTR-P-A2AA) kept locally; the v1.2 update stays a separate comparison input. TARGET.md records the author’s base container SHA-256 3bb3b4eb0d17f18875d8b847c871dc97a172beeda03ce99e59e62a78ed5c1a53 and notes that these hashes identify the supplied dumps, not every copy. Retail containers, extracted code, raw REA dossiers, game frames and emulator logs stay in ignored private directories.

SETUP.md uses Ubuntu WSL on Windows with Node.js 22, Python 3, GCC and readelf. Its bootstrap builds REA from source revision 7ae3c50a9d49c480035855de9fcc4484befacd92 (package version 6.4.0) and runs it with Ghidra 12.1.4 and Temurin JDK 21, with Capstone 5.0.7 as an independent decoder. Rebuilds use a pinned 3DS Decomp Pipeline revision, the C replacements were compiled with Ubuntu’s gcc-arm-none-eabi (GCC 10.3.1), and runtime checks use Azahar 2126.2 and its RPC interface.

The project reports independent byte checks of the unchanged rebuilds, isolated behavior tests and live RPC readbacks for the replaced routines, and 60 passing source-owned tests. Runtime evidence is a bounded startup, setup and bedroom comparison under one input movie; routine execution counts, battles, overworld coverage, full-movie completion and timing determinism remain unverified. The tests use source-owned fixtures, not retail bytes; this collection ran neither the tools nor the game.

README directs agent-accessible analysis through REA and Ghidra and requires AI-assisted reconstructions to be reviewed against binary evidence; AGENTS.md and HANDOFF.md are written for continuing agent sessions, and RUNTIME.md records frame review by an independent reviewing agent. The repository has no license file and GitHub detects none; it describes itself as an independent fan project unaffiliated with Nintendo, Game Freak or The Pokémon Company. No runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: Reversed with AI
description_en: A moderated website directory of AI-assisted reverse-engineering projects across games, firmware, file formats, APIs and protocols, apps and legacy software. Each entry links to its primary source and records the author-reported model, tools, time, cost and outcome, with four checks for public source, reproduction steps, real-hardware testing and third-party confirmation.
description_zh: 经人工审核的网站目录，收录游戏、固件、文件格式、API 与协议、应用及旧软件领域的 AI 辅助逆向项目。每个条目链接一手来源，记录作者报告的模型、工具、耗时、费用与结果，并标注源码公开、复现步骤、真实硬件测试和第三方确认四项检查。
requirements: Reviewed as a live website on 2026-10-18, when the homepage reported 180 projects, 100 marked Works, 12 guides and 166 tools, and the sitemap listed 180 project pages. The site has no pinned revision or public source repository, so entries, counts and labels can change after this review.

Entries record target, model, tools, time, cost, outcome (Works, Partial or Research), a 1–5 human-effort scale and four reproducibility checks. The About page says figures are reported by authors, not measured by the site, and unknown fields are marked Not reported; a Works label is the author’s claim. A Reproducible badge needs Works plus public source and repro steps, with real-hardware or third-party confirmation for firmware and devices.

The policy lists interoperability, preservation, modding that does not bypass DRM or anti-cheat, legacy-software recovery, format, protocol and API documentation, the user’s own devices, CTFs and defensive malware analysis without live samples. It declines DRM, licence-check and anti-cheat bypasses, online cheats, leaked source, live malware samples and weaponised exploits. The site says it hosts no binaries or code and accepts takedown requests; each linked project still needs its own rights and original-asset review.

The maintainer, smyaseen (@whyamas on X), reviews every submission; sponsored placements are labelled, and the site says sponsors do not affect listings or order. Its guides include a third-party REA setup guide updated 2026-10-14, but the directory covers many tools beyond REA and is not an official REA resource. The reviewed pages show a copyright notice and no reuse license for directory content.

name: Notes CSV export: an author-reported REA check of reconstruction oracles
description_en: A Chinese article breaks three versions of a Python CSV exporter that reproduces the Notes teaching app shipped with REA. It shows that a simple export-and-read-back test passes all three, while byte comparisons against the official JavaScript formatter on 215 fixed inputs catch each one. The author also connects REA 6.5.0 over MCP, reruns its JavaScript analysis and checks that an edited evidence record is rejected on import; this is a study of acceptance checks, not a new reconstruction.
description_zh: 一篇中文文章把复刻 REA 自带 Notes 教学应用的 Python CSV 导出器故意改坏三个版本，展示简单的“导出再读回”测试能让三者全部通过，而以官方 JavaScript 格式化函数为参照、在 215 组固定输入上逐字节比较则能逐一识破。作者还通过 MCP 连接 REA 6.5.0，重新运行其 JavaScript 分析，并验证被改动的证据记录在导入时会被拒绝；这是对验收检查的研究，而非新的重建。
requirements: The 2026-10-16 article by @superfang119 follows the author’s earlier walkthrough, in which a Python reimplementation of the Notes app’s CSV export reportedly matched the original byte for byte on 215 inputs. It used Windows, Node 22.19.0 and rea-agents 6.5.0 through a temporary stdio client that listed 207 tools; the JavaScript analysis returned 6 files, 32 nodes and 45 edges. The author notes that this static graph locates the export path but does not show the full Electron app running.

The frozen byte contract quotes every title, doubles inner quotes and ends lines and the file with LF, for safe-integer ids and string titles. Each mutant changes one rule: quoting only when needed, leaving inner quotes unescaped, or dropping the final LF. A one-note read-back test passed all three. Against references from running the official JavaScript formatter on 15 fixed edge cases and 200 seeded inputs, the baseline matched 215/215 and the mutants differed on 26, 166 and 215 inputs.

Changing one evidence field from 6 to 999 while keeping its evidence_id made the same REA server reject the import with evidence_integrity_mismatch and leave session evidence unchanged; the author adds that this detects tampering but cannot show an interpretation is correct. The article also cites, without rerunning it, a TH08 project fix in which a comparator missed a 128.0 constant written as 0.0.

Analysis and implementation ran in the same Codex context, so the author states this is not clean-room separation, and the handoff prompts offered are proposals rather than a tested protocol. Scripts, mutants and outputs are not published, so this collection could not rerun them; the three probes do not cover permissions, write failures, concurrency or the full interface. The target is REA’s own teaching sample, not a third-party product.
